trainers.instruction: Match the fractions that have the same value.

atoms.b: When adding or subtracting fractions with different denominators, a ((++common_denominator common_numerator)) needs to be found.

In order for <mat><t-yellow>4</t-yellow>/<t-purple>5</t-purple></mat> to have the same denominator as <mat><t-yellow>4</t-yellow>/<t-purple>15</t-purple></mat>, we’ll need to multiply the denominator by <mat><gap>++3 5 2</gap></mat>.
To make sure the new fraction is equivalent, you ((only_multiply_the_denominator ++multiply_both_the_numerator_and_the_denominator)) of the fraction.

atoms.sound: twelve fifteenths plus 4 fifteenths equals sixteen fifteenths.
